record.original_question: For a homogeneous elastic body with pure displacement boundary conditions, strictly polyconvex stored-energy function W, and reference domain Ω homeomorphic to a ball, prove or disprove uniqueness of sufficiently smooth equilibrium solutions.

evidence.quote: Problem 8. Prove or disprove the uniqueness of sufficiently smooth equilibrium solutions to pure displacement boundary-value problems for homogeneous bodies when the stored-energy function W is strictly polyconvex and Ω is homeomorphic to a ball.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let Ω ⊂ ℝ^3 be a bounded open set with sufficiently regular boundary that is homeomorphic to the closed unit ball. Consider a homogeneous hyperelastic body occupying Ω in its reference configuration, with stored-energy function W : M^{3×3}_+ → ℝ defined on the set of 3×3 matrices with positive determinant. Assume W is strictly polyconvex, i.e. there exists a strictly convex function G : M^{3×3} × M^{3×3} × (0,∞) → ℝ such that
   W(F) = G(F, cof F, det F)   for all F ∈ M^{3×3}_+,
where cof F denotes the cofactor matrix of F. Given a smooth boundary datum u_0 : ∂Ω → ℝ^3, consider deformations u : Ω → ℝ^3 with det ∇u > 0 satisfying the pure displacement boundary condition u = u_0 on ∂Ω, and the equilibrium equations
   div(DW(∇u)) = 0   in Ω.

Question: Either prove that, among sufficiently smooth (e.g. C^2 up to the boundary) equilibrium solutions u with det ∇u > 0 and u|_{∂Ω} = u_0, there is at most one; or exhibit a counterexample (a strictly polyconvex W, a domain Ω homeomorphic to a ball, and boundary data u_0 admitting at least two distinct smooth equilibrium solutions).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to remain open in the stated generality. Uniqueness is known only under restrictive assumptions: F. John established uniqueness for smooth deformations with uniformly small strains, and K. Zhang showed that for small displacements from a stress-free state the smooth solution obtained by the implicit function theorem is the unique global minimizer. Counterexamples to uniqueness have been constructed on annular (non-simply-connected) two-dimensional domains (e.g. Spadaro 2009), but no resolution is known for domains homeomorphic to a ball with strictly polyconvex W.

status_evidence.title: Non-Uniqueness of Minimizers for Strictly Polyconvex Functionals
status_evidence.snippet: Counterexample with at least two analytic global minimizers, on an annular domain.
status_evidence.claim: Non-uniqueness can occur for strictly polyconvex functionals on non-ball domains.

status_evidence.title: Some Open Problems in Elasticity (J.M. Ball)
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 8: prove or disprove uniqueness of smooth equilibria for pure displacement BVP with strictly polyconvex W on Ω homeomorphic to a ball.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: On the Uniqueness of Minimizers for a Class of Variational Problems with Polyconvex Integrand
status_evidence.snippet: Partial uniqueness results for restricted classes of polyconvex integrands.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial uniqueness results are available.
